Fly-on-the-wall documentary following the men and women who defend Australia from drug runners, smugglers and terrorists. (S4, ep 17)
Fly-on-the-wall documentary following the men and women who defend Australia from drug runners, smugglers and terrorists. (S4, ep 18)

A returning American is cuffed at the Peace Arch crossing in Washington and in Detroit, a German rock band rolls straight into secondary. (S1, ep 13)
At Detroit Metro Airport, a traveller minding manners may need to mind his story instead and the Chicago canine unit knows smugglers don't play games. (S1, ep 14)
Jump in as we witness icy escapades, heart-warming animal rescues and the wrath of ancient Nordic gods against motorcyclists. (S3, ep 7)
A fleeing driver leads police on a chase through the woods and an intense storm adds difficulty to police investigating a shooting. Flashing images. (S2, ep 38)
A smuggling attempt unfolds at the Brisbane Container Examination Facility. Meanwhile, a passenger's unusual behaviour raises alarm bells. (S17, ep 11)
Identical packages at the mail centre raise alarm bells, a passenger goes missing during a bag search and a young man is distraught after being caught. (S17, ep 12)
Officers interrogate a popular woman, a religious figurine may be concealing something sinister and a student from China is on the brink of being sent home. (S17, ep 13)
A man is raising red flags when he arrives in Brisbane. A woman tries to smuggle dangerous goods and officers find some strong 'tea' at the air cargo facility. (S17, ep 14)
From animals taking over the roads, to arguments over parking, we've got it all caught on camera. (S4, ep 4)
Conversion: Dr Beckett realises that the 'retrovirus' Ellia ingested is now in Sheppard's bloodstream... and he's mutating into the very creature that attacked him. (S2, ep 8)
Fair Trade: The ship encounters a region of space named the Nekrit Expanse. Neelix has no knowledge of the space beyond this point, so he calls in a favour from an old friend. (S3, ep 13)
Journey's End: While Picard is forced to relocate a group of American Indians from a planet where they have settled, one of the colonists causes Wesley to re-examine his future.
Hookman: The team track a sniper targeting the police in a must-see remake of a standout episode from the original series. Peter Weller (Robocop) guest stars and directs. (S3, ep 15)
Barry Prudom: Barry sparked Britain's largest manhunt, murdering police officers and civilians. The terror ended when he turned the gun on himself rather than face justice. (S10, ep 7)
David Baxendale: In 2010, Sarah Thomas was stabbed to death in her home. The killer fled abroad and changed his identity. Finally recognised, the truth came to light. (S10, ep 8)
Chupacabra: Nick and Hank investigate a series of horrific murders linked to the legendary Chupacabra. (S4, ep 8)
How do they put the holes in Swiss cheese? How do they restore and improve a classic battle tank? And how do robotic librarians run one of the world's biggest book collections?
How do they persuade an oyster to grow a perfect pearl? How do they put the twist in classic Pennsylvania pretzels? And how do they build Venice's traditional gondolas?
Rare Survivors. Serkan and Jay visit a Victorian steam museum, while Serkan and Alister Dryburgh get to trawl through storage containers at a Kent country house.
Provenance Counts. Serkan, Jay and Viki hunt for items with remarkable history. In Somerset they visit a family-run quarry, and a collection of circus artefacts.
VW Beetle Karmann Cabriolet. Paul and Drew take on their biggest restoration yet, a VW Beetle Karmann Cabriolet. The car is in terrible condition, but Drew is determined to save it.
More everyday items are put under the microscope as we discover how they are made, including levels, hot dogs, abrasive grains and sandpaper.
More everyday items are put under the microscope as we discover how they are made, including ice cream treats, wooden golf clubs and aircraft wings.
Teleshopping.
Teleshopping.
Automata Acrobatics. Automata artisans Michael and Maria restore an acrobatic figurine from France. Meanwhile, sculptor Nick revives a pair of fairground ride motorbikes.
Branching Out. Drew heads to a Kent antiques emporium specialising in unusual European antiques, and indulges in 1940s nostalgia at a home front museum in South West Wales.
Balbithan. Drew goes North of the border on a road trip for an epic private house clearance in a remote part of Scotland, and he visits a historic cutlery factory in Sheffield.
The Poseidon Crew receive devastating news about their mining permits. The Dust Devils gamble big on a quartz reef. Shane and Russell strike gold.
A new crew are under threat from crocodiles and accusations of illegal prospecting. The Victoria Diggers receive some welcome help.
In Deep. The Boulder Boys drain floodwater in search of opals. Rod Manning is under pressure after using his wife's favourite opal ring as collateral.
Machines. The Blacklighters must relocate Opalzilla after their claim runs dry of opal. The Cheals hope to hit the jackpot in a bizarre structure, the Z-fault.
Drew and Tee are excited by the items on offer at the largest antiques market in Italy. And, they visit a picturesque town in Spain to look at a fascinating collection.
Ford Transit. Henry and Fuzz visit Warwickshire to revive a battered Ford Transit. Once a workhorse of Britain, now a rusted relic longing for a second life.
Graham Steeler. Henry and Fuzz head to Southend to visit Graham's shed full of bikes and muscle cars. They find a Dutton kit car and rows and rows of rare bikes.
Will Ralph. Henry and Fuzz visit a farm near Colchester with vintage tractors galore. The boys come away with a classic Fordson and some old traffic lights.

items.t: Find It, Fix It, Flog It
items.sum: Henry and Simon head to High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire to unearth some treasures in the barns. They spot a pair of ornate candle holders and a go-cart.
Dominic Littlewood & Lisa George. In Dom Littlewood's stylish seaside pad, Angus finds a rare guitar. Then, he checks out 1950s treasures at soap star Lisa George's home.
A Lost Masterpiece? Angus spies a treasure whilst helping a couple downsize and turns detective to identify whether a work of art is by a very famous artist or not.
Mysterious Girl. In the border towns of Scotland and England, who is the mysterious lady in the photograph, and will a parrot make the journey home?
Tristan. In Chelmsford, Henry and Fuzz visit Fiat specialist Tristan, who has 500s, 600s, 126s and a Fiat minivan that once starred in an Indiana Jones movie.
Dominic. The boys are in Oxfordshire browsing through Dominic's restoration projects, including a Triumph TR4, a Jaguar XJS and a hotrod with a Rover engine.
Road To Redemption. Opalton Boulder Crew are going to the Winton Opal Festival, Slim Pickings are finally at White Peg, and the Mooka Boys have driven to Coober Pedy.
Furniture restorer Will attempts to help Katherine and John who have an heirloom that's been deemed unusable. Can Will bring this beautiful piece back to life?
Japanese scientists stimulate oysters to form perfect pearls. Handcrafted pretzels are made with a twist. Workers maintain the craft of the gondolier.
Roulette wheels are made to be perfectly unpredictable. The secrets behind the purest olive oil are revealed. An old wreck is made into the Batmobile.
Self-professed 'crazy camel lady' Sandra wants a mature man to ride off into the sunset with. Pansexual erotic writer Toni-Ann dreams of being the heroine in her own sexy novel.
Three daters return to the restaurant hoping for better luck second time around, while some couples who had great dates return - and one of them gets down on bended knee...
The Goggleboxers have been watching The Crown, Survivor, 007: Road to a Million, The Good Ship Murder and Shoplifters: Caught Red Handed.
Brand new series - Alex: Jacob is shocked to find out that his colleagues aren't invested in his frequent email messages. Gregory turns to Janine for help with a former student.
Treehouse of Horror XXIV: In three spine-tingling stories, Homer rhymes in a Dr Seuss-style tale, Bart is beheaded in a kite-flying prang, and a travelling circus visits town.
Bottle Episode: Homer must transport a million-dollar bottle of wine to Mr Burns's mansion. And for once, it's not actually him who screws it up.
Spaceballs: Adam tries to start a Mel Brooks club after watching the movie Spaceballs. Erica plans to tell Beverly and Pops about a big decision she's made.
Let's Val Kilmer This Car: When Lainey turns down Barry's invitation to take her to the prom, he plans a prank with Principal Ball's car to get out of going.
Express Yourself: Phil has the crazy idea of going on a spontaneous trip to Paris with Claire. And Jay takes over their bathroom renovation.
Man Shouldn't Lie: Claire brings home a stray dog and gets the kids to help her hide it. And Cameron rents out the upstairs apartment to a Christian rock band.
Strangers in the Night: When Alex tells Phil and Claire she has a boyfriend, they worry that they've put too much pressure on her and that she's made up an imaginary boyfriend.
Haley's 21st Birthday: The family take Haley to a bar to celebrate her 21st birthday. Can Claire convince Haley to see her as a friend, rather than as her uptight mum?
A short, cheeky clip from Rude Tube's naughty little sister, Rude(ish) Tube, featuring sports of the lawnmower, motorbike and bicycle variety.
In Bournemouth, David and AJ plan a South African menu - with bread in every course. Vinnie and Alex serve South American dishes. And Andrea and Wayne's Vietnamese night doesn't go to plan.
Gordon Ramsay revisits three restaurants to find out if they've continued to follow his advice. How have Down City, Classic American and Davide fared in his absence?
Gordon Ramsay revisits four restaurants he tried to help: the Spanish Pavillion in New Jersey, and Kingston Café, La Frite and Capri in California.
The two series winners compete to win a cruise holiday. Plus: people unintentionally do the splits. And more. Alfonso Ribeiro hosts.
Banks Shot: When Will gets hustled in a pool hall and almost loses the family car, Uncle Phil comes to his rescue and outhustles the hustlers.
72 Hours: Carlton accepts Will's challenge to survive for two days in a tough LA neighbourhood.
The Bart Wants What It Wants: Rainier Wolfcastle's daughter (guest star Reese Witherspoon) develops a crush on Bart.
The Lastest Gun in the West: Bart befriends a cowboy who used to be a film star and tries to help him regain his fame. But he isn't prepared for his new hero's love of booze.
The Flandshees of Innersimpson: Flanders vows never to speak to Homer again after Homer steals his new headphones. Homer's absolutely delighted - at first...
Blame It on Lisa: The Simpsons go to Brazil to meet an orphan who Lisa has secretly been writing to. But as soon as they arrive, Homer is kidnapped.
Sixteen Candles: Murray and Beverly forget Adam's 16th birthday.
You Got Zuko'd: Adam's girlfriend Jackie returns from her summer in New York but acts like a different person. Beverly is unhappy with Lainey's culinary skills.
Double-Click: Claire can't seem to find the right time to fire an employee, Phil thinks he caught Luke with a girl in his bed, and no one notices that Alex has moved back.
A Tale of Three Cities: There's a reunion after trips took the Dunphys to New York; Mitch, Cam and Lily to the Midwest; and Jay, Gloria, Manny and Joe to Juarez in Mexico.
A Stereotypical Day: Jay goes out of his way to make a good impression on the new neighbours.
Blindsided: The Dunphys and Pritchetts go head-to-head when Luke decides his best chance of getting into college is to run against Manny in the senior class president election.
Yellow Subterfuge: Bart becomes a model student so that he can go on a school trip on a submarine. But Principal Skinner has other ideas...
White Christmas Blues: When radioactive steam from the nuclear power plant mixes with pollution, snow falls over Springfield and the town is inundated with holiday revellers.
Steal This Episode: Irked by high cinema ticket prices, Homer starts screening pirated movies in his back garden. But the FBI soon catch up with him...
Married to the Blob: Comic Book Guy asks Homer for advice on how to woo cute comic fan Kumiko, who visits his shop to research material for an autobiographical manga.
The Great Money Caper: When Homer leaves Bart by the squid port, kind strangers start giving money to the 'street urchin'. So Homer and Bart turn to a life of scamming.
Brand new series - 2 Ava 2 Fest: Ava Fest is back, and with the help of the teachers, Ava's determined to outdo last year by any means necessary.
The Big Four-Oh: When Vivian turns 40, she becomes obsessed with achieving her lifelong dream of being a professional dancer.
She Ain't Heavy: Will takes the shallow way out when his friends tease him about his date (guest star Queen Latifah).
What do Britain's top armchair critics think of Squid Game: The Challenge, The Couple Next Door, The Toy Hospital, Survivor, Vinnie Jones in the Country and Lorraine?
What do the Goggleboxers think of Squid Game: The Challenge, The Couple Next Door, Strictly Come Dancing, The Graham Norton Show, Planet Earth III, and Jingle All the Way?
David and Natalie's keepers both get incredibly possessive when their new suitors enter the house, leading to some very, very awkward conversations.
(2008) Stark drama. Young villagers in the Cotswolds turn to heroin to fill their empty days and empty lives. Sexual scenes/strong language/hard drug use.
Teleshopping.
Teleshopping.
(1951) Second World War drama. Richard Widmark stars as a commanding officer leading US Marines into the Pacific to capture Japanese prisoners and discover the location of a rocket base.
(1955) Romantic drama with Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson. A wealthy widow decides to restart her life. But her children and her social set disapprove of her lover, forcing her to rethink.
(1944) Alfred Hitchcock's Oscar-nominated Second World War drama starring Tallulah Bankhead, William Bendix and Walter Slezak as three of the survivors from a liner torpedoed by the Nazis.
(1957) Offbeat melodrama starring Richard Burton (as an RAF officer), Joan Collins (as a nun), Basil Sydney and Cy Grant, who end up on a life raft together after their ship is torpedoed.
Writer/director Martin McDonagh and cast discuss the Film4-produced political comedy thriller Wild Horse Nine.
(1996) Helen Hunt, Bill Paxton and Philip Seymour Hoffman star in writer Michael Crichton's tornado-chasing action adventure about a bunch of clever misfits hunting the perfect storm.
(1985) Thriller starring Arnold Schwarzenegger. To free his kidnapped daughter, an ex US commando must agree to assassinate a South American president. But he's not as pliant as he seems...
(2022) Ti West's acclaimed grindhouse horror with Mia Goth. Some adult filmmakers inexplicably choose a ramshackle house in the Bible-Belt wilderness to shoot a film. It's gonna get nasty.
Stable Cottage Buntingford. The team are called in to investigate sinister activity at a grade 2 listed cottage. The residents are increasingly disturbed by unexplainable events. S2, Ep2
Little Easton Manor. The team investigate a picturesque mansion in a small village in Essex. Can they find the cause of the reported strange sounds and apparitions? S2, Ep3
Teleshopping.
Scotland Special. Drew gets an insider's tour of Scotland with local dealer, Viki Knott. He discovers a Mackintosh-influenced chair and some sinister 1960s Americana. S18, Ep10
Different Is Good. Drew and Alister are on the hunt for exciting stock. They visit a business specialising in the creation of artificial flowers for film and theatre. S18, Ep11
Gaby Roslin helps IT girl and socialite Victoria Hervey find her dream countryside retreat near Windsor. She has a budget of £800,000 for her peaceful home. S1, Ep6
Your one-stop-shop for all things cruise; bringing you the hottest destinations, ground-breaking ships and the latest deals to ensure your next cruise is your greatest one!
Episode 94. British couples seek to swap grey skies for sun, sea and sand abroad. With the help of property experts, can they find the home of their dreams? S1, Ep14
Drew is on a road trip, travelling to Norfolk, Pembroke and Essex. In Pembroke, he finds an old church that has been converted into an antiques store with a varied selection. S13, Ep3
In a quiet South London suburb, Drew comes face to face with the most extraordinary collection of American automobilia he's ever seen, including Evel Knievel's Messerschmitt. S13, Ep4
His hunt for fresh stock takes Drew to the Cotswolds, where he finds a giant stash of Indian and Afghan treasures which have come directly from the subcontinent. S13, Ep5
Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon continue their adventure with the end destination of Christchurch. Catherine finds an interesting croquet set and biscuit tin along the way. S13, Ep12
Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon continue their journey as they travel through the West Country on the hunt for some serious bargains. S13, Ep13
Horologist Steve fixes a very precious clock in the shape of a ship. Meanwhile, ceramics expert Kirsten is challenged with restoring a damaged bird bath. S6, Ep57
Treading New Ground. Treading new ground across the UK, Drew and Viki explore the factory complex of a historic British cloth producer and a sprawling reclamation yard. S18, Ep12
Conversation Starters. Drew and Alister's hunt for pieces with an interesting backstory takes them from Sussex to Shropshire with campaign furniture and quirky collectables. S18, Ep13
Alex comes to the rescue of a dog-friendly village pub in Wiltshire. The owner is on the brink of burnout and the business is no longer profitable. S13, Ep4
Sarah Moore rescues an unwanted bureau, an old church noticeboard and a broken extending table from Witley recycling centre in Surrey. S15, Ep11
From Russia With Love. A widow returns from Italy, bringing with her Soviet propaganda. While Victorian gadgets sees Angus geek-out over tech from a bygone age. S4, Ep20
Izzie Balmer and James Braxton are on the hunt for interesting items in Foulsham. James buys a Victorian plant stand, while Izzie eyes a bamboo mirror. S19, Ep14
Now. Destinee & Dynastiee - Part 1. Identical twins Destinee and Dynastiee weigh over 1200 pounds combined. They determine to get healthy and lose weight together with Dr. Now's help. S1, Ep8
I Can't Smile. Brenda is paralysed down one side of her face and desperately wants her smile back. Plus, surgeon Vijay attempts a difficult procedure to straighten Meghan's jaw. S1, Ep6
Smugglers Inn. In Sussex, the team investigate a historic inn with a gruesome past. The new owners ignored the dark reputation, but strange phenomena are giving them second thoughts. S2, Ep4
In Hertfordshire, the heli-medics help a man who is fighting for his life following a cardiac arrest. And fun-runner Vijitha suffers a painful open fracture.
Some patients at King's have obvious symptoms while others initially baffle the medical team. Consultant Graham thinks Icylyn's bloated abdomen could be due to something serious.
Bobby, 48, is brought to King's by his partner after having seizures at home. Ronald, 70, is having problems breathing. Rienelle, who's seven, has fallen and landed on her back.
Jo and Ellis want a holiday home on Spain's Costa Blanca, where they can spend their time enjoying water sports and mountain biking. Laura Hamilton shows them what their £60k can buy.
Teleshopping with High Street TV
Teleshopping with High Street TV
David and Giles take a modern approach to running their B&B, Langland Road, in the Mumbles, near Swansea. But not all of their guests can work out the high-tech offerings.
Margaret runs the Castle Lodge Hotel in Felixstowe to exacting standards, but not all of the guests are pleased with the decor and there's some horsing around during the group outing.
Gordon and Sandra host at Bryn Woodlands House in Colwyn Bay, where they take their guests harness racing. But how will one guest react to finding a snake in his bed?
Edward and Rachel offer some showbiz razzmatazz at The Tollemache Arms in Cheshire. But the show's nearly over at breakfast when Ed ruins the eggs and sets fire to a towel.
It's the final day of the competition and the B&Bers meet for one last time to settle some scores and find out how much they've been paid. Tensions run high before the winner is announced.
Sheffield area. The first host, chocolate shop manager and self-confessed party animal Ginnette, plans a feast of fun family favourites and surprise entertainment. (Ep1/5)
Sheffield area. Emergency services worker Josh plans to impress his guests with an evening of high-end nosh and saucy sketching. But is his main too spicy? (Ep2/5)
Sheffield area. GP surgery manager Clare serves up a winter warmer menu featuring perfect presentation and hearty portions, while guest Andy lays on his best jokes. (Ep3/5)
Sheffield area. Wellness coach Andy, a 'secret' foodie, hopes to strike the right balance with some tasty and nutritious grub. But will his singing pass the test? (Ep4/5)
Sheffield area. Psychologist Abi hosts the final night with a travel-inspired Asian menu, a lesson in sock puppetry, and some controversial burning-hot chilli sauce. (Ep5/5)
Karen and her son Liam welcome their rivals to the luxurious Jockhedge Holiday Cottages in Burgh le Marsh, Lincolnshire. But not everything lives up to the high-end price tag...
Carolynne and her son George have high hopes for their brand-new B&B, The Victoria Inn in Witton-le-Wear, County Durham. But one guest gets locked in the loo and breakfast gets a bashing.
Aidan and Mij host at the Earlston House Hotel in Paignton, Devon. One guest gets a bum deal with the loo roll and, at breakfast, there's kitchen confusion and sausage snobbery.
The final visit is to Pete's Beach House in Portland, Dorset. But his back-to-basics B&B doesn't do it for everyone, and Karen and Liam's feedback really gets Pete's goat.
It's the final day of the competition. After scores are settled on everything from sleepless nights to smelly showers, the payments are revealed and the winner is announced.
Everything Must Go: On the trail of two vintage Harley-Davidsons in Pennsylvania, Frank gets more than he bargained for when one bike collector takes a liking to him!
When Georgie meets Diaz, it's a dream come true... but is the energetic pup too much for mum Deb to handle? A family of dog novices struggle to form a connection.
Lexi seeks a bedtime buddy. Jasmine wants a pooch now her twin sister's off to uni. And a rare cross of lurcher and old English sheepdog helps a priest find his inner silliness.

items.t: The Secret Life of the Zoo
items.sum: Vila the chimp makes a bid for the job of top female but gets hurt in a fight with rival Alice. And Chester Zoo's super-rare pink pigeons need to stop arguing and start mating.
Brand new series: Piglet fires the world's last remaining T3 steam engine in Dorset. A bridge repair faces a setback, and Omaha's coal-to-oil conversion reaches a key moment.
Kevin, who's 78, is rushed to A&E after going into cardiac arrest while exercising. Monica, who's 83 and has osteoporosis, has been rushed to King's after falling at home.
A look at the work of the King's stroke team, who treat over 1300 patients a year. And the UK's over-40s BMX champion visits A&E after falling 20 feet when a stunt went wrong.
The unsparing panel show that puts the mockers on the world's headline-makers. This 'best of' end-of-series special also features riotous new material and daft outtakes.
Compilation: Rob Brydon returns with a special episode of the rib-tickling, fib-tackling comedy panel show, featuring all the best outtakes and unseen bits from series 7.
Christmas Special: The jolly panel show goes all Christmassy as Miranda Hart, Stephen Mangan, Barry Cryer and Miles Jupp join the three wise regulars.
Rhonda, Diana, Jake and Trent: Eleanor and the gang make their way to the Bad Place headquarters, to plead their case to spend eternity in the Good Place.

items.t: Dave Gorman: Modern Life Is Goodish
items.sum: Will It Make Toasters Cheaper?: Mr Gorman brings the curtain down on his cheeky comedy series about the world we live in, examining the role of faith in modern life.
Psychiatrist and author Philippa Perry joins comedians Nabil Abdulrashid, Luke Kempner, and Sarah Millican as they take on the best-selling author's quizzing challenges.
Shopping from Home.
Shopping from Home.
Jeremy test drives a Koenigsegg, the boys create the world's first convertible people carrier, and Jimmy Carr and Alan Davies are among the guests.
Officers on Skye are tipped off about a resident suspected of possessing an illegal weapon, and dangerous winds in Harris cause a road traffic incident.

items.t: Special Ops: To Catch a Criminal
items.sum: Operation Inuit: The Thames Valley Major Crime Unit investigate a tragic murder on the eve of Valentine's Day - fuelled by jealousy, anger and pride, it's a tale of love gone wrong.
Rick takes us to the place where his passion for Cornwall began - his family home at Trevose Head on the north Cornish coast, where he would go fishing with his father as a child.
Rick takes us to meet an extraordinary family who are making some of the best Gouda cheese in Britain and discovers the origins of the sea shanty in the fishing village of Mevagissey.
Rick meets young chef Tom Adams, who runs Combeshead Farm, a leading field-to-fork restaurant in Cornwall. Rick then tries out a new recipe - pork chops with a sloe berry sauce.
Rick discovers an unusual superstition and a rare type of Norman castle in Launceston, before meeting musicians Graham Fitkin and Ruth Wall in the far west of Cornwall.
A Taste of the Med: The bikers continue their journey through time, celebrating British grub. Here, they look at the influence of the Mediterranean on British cuisine.
Venice: Timothy West and Prunella Scales embark on a spectacular canal journey to Venice, beginning 14 miles west of the Italian city on the Brenta.
Motoring news and views with those car-crazed chums. Jeremy tests out the Dodge Viper and Richard tries out some incredible prototypes. Joanna Lumley is their fabulous guest.
Hydroplaning Bike: The motorbike racer and mechanic heads to Bala Lake to try to set the world record for riding a motorcycle on the surface of water.

Rick takes us to meet an extraordinary family who are making some of the best Gouda cheese in Britain and discovers the origins of the sea shanty in the fishing village of Mevagissey.

Bruno Tonioli, Adam Buxton, Kirsty Wark and Rob Beckett join brazen bluffers David Mitchell and Lee Mack to tell tall tales and uncomfortable truths. Rob Brydon presents.
Bob Mortimer and Mel Giedroyc are amongst the stars revealing improbable titbits about themselves, some of which are untrue. Can their fellow celebs pick out the porkies?
Lee Mack, David Mitchell, Miles Jupp, Heston Blumenthal, Emilia Fox and Ed Byrne try to separate tall tale from candid confession in the wily panel show. Rob Brydon hosts.
Occupations and Offices: Sandi Toksvig hosts a light-hearted look into Occupations and Offices with Deirdre O'Kane, Richard Osman, David Mitchell and Alan Davies.

items.t: Have I Got a Bit More News for You
items.sum: Roy Wood Jr is host as comedian and actor Guz Khan - and broadcaster Kirsty Wark - join team captains Paul Merton and Ian Hislop to delve into the news.
We Met At Mealtimes: The competitors use their ingenuity with snowy globes, rubbery ducks and wooden-y spoons to impress Taskmaster Greg Davies.
A Killing Kindness: The Beeb's hit series of mysteries, adapted from the novels of Reginald Hill. The duo must unravel the enigmatic words of Shakespeare's Hamlet to solve a case.
Stars on Sunday: Classic comedy from the TV husband and wife who were so convincing many people thought they were married in real life. The couple visit Terry's boss in hospital.
A Botox a Day Keeps the Mortician in Pay: When a hen party ends in murder, Harry and Fergus are hired by the bridezilla to make sure her big day goes ahead without a hitch.
Shopping from Home.
Shopping from Home.
For Better and Worse: Polly Page investigates the mysterious disappearance of a woman who later turns out to be the bigamous wife of two violent ex-convicts.
The End of the Line: When she is roped into some emergency babysitting, Ruth finds herself questioning her neighbour Danny's suitability for parenthood.
Once Upon a Time: Zara uncovers a girl's dark secret, Cherry's nightmare looks far from over when DI Lucas arrives, and the new consulting room is unveiled but fails to impress.
Bitter from the Sweet: Donna and Mark's medical expertise is needed when they catch up with James and his abductors and have to fight for his life.
Learning to Fly: Jeff discovers that Samantha has been keeping a big secret from him when he meets her husband. The two men soon come to blows - but then someone grabs a kitchen knife.
For Better and Worse: Polly Page investigates the mysterious disappearance of a woman who later turns out to be the bigamous wife of two violent ex-convicts.
As Jack and Carol wait at Amy's bedside a hungover Roxy returns to the Square, unaware of what has happened. Meanwhile, Phil tells Ben and Jay to get their stories straight.
Yusef finds himself with a surprising ally as he struggles to gain Zainab's forgiveness. The Mitchells support Roxy when she becomes homeless and faces a future without Amy.
Daphne prepares for her wedding with Des Clarke, and Madge Mitchell starts her job answering calls for Clive Gibbons and his gorillagram service. Helen's niece Nikki visits.
Zoe Davis buys a scratchcard and ends up winning $1000, so she pays Shane Ramsay his money back. At No 24 Ramsay Street, Madge Mitchell and her brother Max Ramsay argue.
O Thou Invisible Spirit of Wine: When paranormal activity is reported in a Tudor pub, old family feuds are brought to a head.
The Labyrinth of the Minotaur: The sleuthing priest is asked to look after Lady Felicia's wayward niece Bunty, who soon finds herself suspected of murder.
It's a Knockout: An evening of dressing up in old 'It's A Knockout' costumes coincides with the arrival of Terry's company chairman for dinner. Laughs with the charming couple.
The Crowcroft Challenge: The world's longest-running, silliest sitcom! Alvin soon discovers that it isn't easy travelling as the crow flies, especially when dressed as a crow.
Must Be Good Dancer: More silver-haired shenanigans in rural Yorkshire. Smiler is known for being strictly non-dancing, but this presents a problem with the woman of his dreams.
Howard Remembers Where He Left His Bicycle Pump: Gentle comedy that first graced our screens in 1973. An embarrassed Howard bumps into a female acquaintance from his past.
Dead and Buried: Mick and Shazia investigate the discovery of a Viking hoard after a museum curator is suspicious about the circumstances and summons Mick for a second opinion.
Pistols at Dawn - Part 1: Anais' off-the-books investigation into Maja's murder takes on a new dynamic when Kylie refuses to stay on the sidelines and insists on helping.
Powerhouse: Dennis Waterman and James Bolam are among the ageing detectives in the popular crime drama. The team probe the case of one of the last men to be hanged in Britain.

Queensland's Tropical Coast: Delve into the incredible collection of UFO stories of first-hand witnesses, from flying saucers to strange encounters in sugar cane fields. (S1, ep 1)
Tasmania, New Zealand and the Bass Strait: Investigating the disappearance of pilot Frederick Valentich, whose last transmission gives an account of what he experienced. (S1, ep 2)
Queensland & Papua New Guinea: Travel to Queensland's farming country where rain-drenched crops meet the Great Barrier Reef. Is there a link between water and UFO activity? (S1, ep 3)
Melbourne & Regional Victoria: Explore Melbourne's long history of UFO sightings and hear incredible first-hand accounts from Victoria's locals of otherworldly encounters. (S1, ep 4)
Pawns of Anarchy: Rick gets his hands on a stellar coin but Corey flips out about the sizeable asking price. Meanwhile, Chum deals with an epic NWA Championship Wrestling belt.
Yo! Mary Raps: There are surprises in store in Dallas, where Mary reveals a very different side to her personality. A discovery leads Ricky and Bubba to a den of deviance. (S5, ep 10)
Hands Off Embroidery: Fort Worth witnesses a showdown when Cowboy Matt begins throwing his weight around. Jenny wins a locker containing a very strange item. (S5, ep 11)
Your Pawpaw Loves You!: Lisa gets nostalgic as she returns to Moreno Valley, while Kenny welcomes a new granddaughter to the clan and searches for the perfect unit. (S15, ep 14)
Strings & Beans: Ivy takes on a supervisory role in Stanton which leads him to some Slavic success, while Brandi tries to help Danielle decorate her new apartment. (S15, ep 15)
Aliens And Forbidden Islands: Experts investigate why so many UFOs have been spotted near remote islands. Could these far-removed spots be the earthly homes of aliens? (S6, ep 1)
Ancient UFOs: From the lore and history of ancient Egypt to the myths of Native Americans, mankind's past is riddled with the evidence of UFOs. (S1, ep 5)
Deathbed Confessions: Many believe that extraterrestrial secrets are not just limited to the military - so could deathbed confessions provide evidence of the existence of UFOs? (S1, ep 6)

Join antiques expert and presenter David Dickinson as more collectors try to sell their items to dealers. Will they strike a deal or take a chance at auction instead? (S9, ep 11)

Episode 3: A South Yorkshire man is left with mysterious injuries after a close encounter, while photos hint at an alien crash in Australia. (S1, ep 3)
What Lies Beneath: Sometimes the strangest things on Earth are happening just below the surface. These are the weird and wonderful tales of the secrets that lurk beneath us. (S1, ep 9)

items.sum: 1946. Drama. Director: Lewis Milestone. Stars Barbara Stanwyck, Van Heflin, Lizabeth Scott & Kirk Douglas. The relationships formed in childhood by three friends lead to murder and obsessive love.

items.sum: 1962. A look at the arguments for and against building by-passes, featuring Transport Minister Ernest Marples. With a look at the by-passes being built and the effects on small towns and villages.
The Renegades. Wayne Rogers & Robert Bray run a stagecoach line in the Old West, where they come across a wide variety of killers, robbers and ladies in distress.
Hizzonner the Penguin. 1966. Stars Adam West & Burgess Meredith. Suspiciously endearing himself to the citizens of Gotham by foiling a robbery, the Penguin announces he is running for mayor.
Dizzonner the Penguin. 1966. Stars Adam West, Burgess Meredith & Woodrow Parfrey. The Penguin kidnaps members of the election board in an attempt to sway the votes to become mayor in his favour.
Alfred Hitchcock defined his own unique style of filmmaking from the early days of the 39 Steps and the Lodger to the Hollywood glamour of North by Northwest.
1955. Drama. After the death of her father while motor racing, the daughter (Rona Anderson) is dissuaded from selling his garage by fellow racer Larry (Paul Carpenter) who helps her run it.
Desert Mice. Talking Pictures was fortunate to film with Liz Fraser and discuss her life in film a few years ago. Here she talks exclusively to Robert Ross.
1959. Comedy. Set in WW2, this is the story of an ENSA troupe of entertainers. Starring Sid James, Dora Bryan, Alfred Marks and Liz Fraser.
1953. Comedy. Penniless couple Roger (Bernard Braden) and Jean (Barbara Kelly) will get £10,000 if Roger can live a sober and profitable life. Starring Reg Dixon and John Laurie.
1950. Mystery. Directors: Antony Darnborough & Terence Fisher. Stars Jean Simmons & Dirk Bogarde. Two siblings visit Paris for the Great Exhibition of 1889 when one of them goes missing.
One Night's Grace. 1976. Stars Gemma Jones, Christopher Cazenove & Sally Osborne. Everyone is intrigued when an attractive young lady asks to see Lord Haslemere. Who is she and what is she after?
1955. Drama. Director: Edward Dmytryk. Stars Deborah Kerr, Van Johnson & John Mills. In WW2 London, a writer falls in love with the wife of a civil servant. Both men suspect her of infidelity.
1952. Mystery. Director: Francis Searle. Stars Richard Carlson, Greta Gynt & Herbert Lom. US sleuth Whispering Smith arrives in London on holiday but soon becomes embroiled in a murder case.
An Edinburgh Volcano. 1981. Tom visits Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh, the most studied volcano in the world and where the very beginnings of geology were laid by Edinburgh geologist James Hutton.
The Guilt Beneath the Gingerbread. 1974. Stars Richard Easton, Bill Treacher & Timothy Carlton. Brian finds himself alone to answer police questioning. Meanwhile, unrest at the depot continues.
Man About To Die. 1958. Stars Donald Gray & Neil McCallum. The hero of a children's sci-fi programme on television is a man without enemies, or so he thinks until someone threatens his life.

The world's largest particle collider malfunctions and opens a portal to a nightmare dimension.

(2017) Thriller starring Hannah Barefoot. After surviving a train wreck, a married woman loses her memory. As the pieces of her old life start to come together, will the truth tear her apart?

When a former co-host works his way back into the life of popular TV host Naomi Spencer, the show's success skyrockets, but Naomi's personal life begins to fall apart. Starring Chrishell Stause (2019)

(2019) Thriller with Samaire Armstrong. A teenage girl returns home years after disappearing, but joy is short lived when suspicious character start following her every move.
After wrongly supporting a man who later turned out to be a serial killer, journalist Kate Fisher rebuilds her career but is stalked by someone from her past. Melissa George stars. (2010)
(2018) Drama thriller starring Chelsea Hobbs. Crime fiction becomes a horrifying reality when a novelist's daughter is abducted in a copycat scenario taken straight from her latest book.
(2016) High-flying action with Dina Meyer, Victoria Pratt and Justin Johnson Cortez. An FBI agent's flight is about to get bumpy as her mysterious seat mate forces her to make a life-or-death choice.
(2011) Explosive sci-fi with Richard Burgi. When the dormant supervolcano under Yellowstone National Park erupts, millions of lives are at risk. Can Rangers Charlie and Kate save the day?

In the Scottish Borders, Rosi and Antony bring their farmhouse ceiling down. And in Orpington, Naomi and Shemar get started on the reno of their 1930s semi.

Wendy and Andrew want to buy a place in the pretty whitewashed villages of Andalucía for their £217k. When they see a townhouse they've already viewed, will they love it second time round?

Colour Catastrophe. The heroes set out on a quest to find out who is draining colour from the forest and muster all their positivity to save it from greyness.

items.sum: Whistle to the Beat. Boy's nose makes a weird whistling sound when he is asleep.
19/11/2026. Topical news magazine for children.
Thermal Shock! Seeking a source of heat, Grizzy moves into a greenhouse - but the Lemmings are coming too!
Primitive Activities. The Lemmings dream up a scheme where Grizzy would submit to their will.
Man Ray Returns. Man Ray rents Squidward's house.
Babysitter. Duck soon learns that he is a terrible babysitter, but it seems kids love Frog!
Garden Centre. When his beloved plant is sold by mistake, Duck must lose his job at the garden centre in order to retrieve it from a top-security greenhouse.
Nice Day for an Odd Wedding. The Odd Squad go undercover at a villain wedding to stop the guests from creating mass oddness.
You Could Live on the Moon? Some day people will live on the moon - find out just what they are in for.
...Olds: Maths - Large Number Placement. Learn about counting in thousands and placing value in four digits.
Episode 8. Historical sketch show. A Celtic farmer isn't terribly keen on plans for Hadrian's Wall, and the brainy pioneers of transportation sing about their inventions.
Killers. Steve Backshall has encountered some incredible animals on his search around the planet, including those that are deadly to humans. They're looked at in detail here.
Big Burps! The doctors find out why we burp and film Dr Xand burping from the inside. They also get behind the wheel to discover what it takes to be a good ambulance driver.
Go Faster Pasta. Buddy and BMXer Lakey race to the finish line making chicken and pea-sto pasta.
Episode 10. Dr Chris and Dr Xand find out all about sharks. Chris Packham discovers magnetic sharks and also attempts a terrifying experiment with some reef sharks at the bottom of the ocean.
Engineering Den. Ciarän from Barnsley wants an engineering den where he can create his own inventions.
Veggie Day. The brothers are delivering healthy greens to all the animals. Tyler's puzzle gives the lemurs food for thought - and who will win the bug hotel build challenge?
Can You Cook It? It's on with the aprons as the girls go head-to-head in the kitchen and compete to make a new meal for the school menu.
Reks to the Rescue. Goalie Reks steps up to play for the Spurs cerebral palsy men's team. Riley and Maddie join the under-15s, and Ledley King is in Skill Showdown.
The Walrus Chief. Animated deep sea adventures with Captain Barnacles and his band of explorers. When Peso's precious medical kit is taken, Barnacles and Kwazii try to get it back.
When Dad Sleepwalked. Cosima and Big Lizard investigate the cause of Dad's mysterious sleepwalking in an adventure that takes them around Proxima and right back home again.
Gone Bird. Exhausted with requests for help, Looph deliberately disappears. The Piris turn detective, searching the berg with little success until her ingenious plan is finally revealed.
Hobby. Wizz is desperate for the audience and his friends not to discover his secret hobby.
Factory. Frog creates chaos in a loo roll factory, leaving Duck covered in toilet paper. Duck just wants to fix the machine, but Frog is convinced he's a spooky mummy!

items.t: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
items.sum: Dog's Show. A dog show is coming up, and cool prizes are given to the winning dog and its trainer.
Down to Time. The team try to get their full-out to time, but Angel struggles. Heath worries Jax is ashamed of their friendship, and Layla gets upset with Damian.
Brazil. Steve Backshall only needs two more animals to complete his Deadly 60 list, so he visits the rainforests of Brazil on the trail of the final contenders.
Shirleyverse, Part 2. Everything that Shaun knows and loves comes into question as he impulsively makes a wish that leads to some unexpected consequences.
The Order of the Golden Sausage. Dennis leads the gang on the baffling trail of a mysterious Beanotown secret society.
From Duck to Dawn. Animated series. Count Duckula is back, and he is determined to take over the world, one terrible TV show at a time.
Elf Help. The heroes must quest to get help from the wood elves, but Twinkle struggles to contain her irritation with their high-and-mighty ways.

Shoelaces Rule. Pablo feels tense every time somebody asks him to tie his shoelaces. Even though he really wants to, he can't tie them until those feelings have passed.
Undying Destiny, Part 2. Vlad is deeply in love with Tatiana, the Transylvanian monster hunter - not the best idea!

A Mystery-Solving Gang Divided! The gang come face to face with the ghost of Abraham Lincoln.
The Case of the Video Game Takeover. Maya and Max must rescue Millie after she gets trapped in her favourite video game.
Weekend At Buddy's. After Cody's best friend doll breaks on their watch, Owen and Beth try to fix things.
Broadway Bros. Curtain up for the Broadway Bros! The bros sing and dance with West End star Lucie Jones, before swapping the stage for the water and becoming swans!
Time to Shine. The girls' choir enter the nationals, the Joseph cast list drops, and West End star Kaylen prepares for his opening night as Young Simba in the Lion King.
Giant Sea Lions and Chilean Bullfrog. Steve Backshall heads to Chile in search of giant frogs and feisty sea lions.
This Is CBeebies. Programmes start at 6.00am.
Anther. It's a busy day in the park. The Nogglins explore to find another Tiny Wonder when they discover something sticky. As they investigate, Nono gets too close and ends up needing a bath.
Gooseberry. Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it's Gooseberry singing a song about everything you have to do to become a Gooseberry Club member.
Blankie. Children's animation. Bing inadvertently pees on his blankie. Fortunately, his Hoppity Voosh toy has a cape just as soft and huggy, and it even smells just right too.
Red. Preschool series. A red balloon floats into Teletubbyland and Po leads the tubby phone dance in a special episode about Po's favourite colour.
Tee's Shop. With a little help from Mo, Tee decides to set up his own shop and sell his old and broken toys.
Pink. Fun Pink arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour pink with the Colourblocks!
Strong Potion. Bingo has taken a magic strength potion so that she can lift Dad with ease.
Names. Pando has an earworm, and Bing isn't impressed.
Wingsuit Yourself. Tao needs help learning to fly his new wingsuit for a big town event, and Mojo and Bo are the experts. Can they help him find his inner bird before it's too late?
The Wish Badge. Whilst helping Duggee clean up, the Squirrels come across an old lamp. Duggee explains that many years ago, when rubbed, it could grant three magical wishes.
The List Badge. Duggee's lost his list for the day's activities at Squirrel Club.
Magic. Bluey teaches Bingo how to use magic so she can make Mum play with her.
Ice Cream. Bluey and Bingo try to taste each other's each ice creams, but they're starting to melt.
Plain of Jars, Laos. Kym must master the G.O. Jump Click-On to protect the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos from a giant Grandmaster Glitch.
The Tale of the Squeaky Toy. Animated series. When Peter loses Cotton-tail's beloved squeaky rabbit toy, he must run the gauntlet of his enemies to get it back!
Snowshoe Hares. When winter comes early in Canada, the Octonauts help some hares with their camouflage.
Number Rescue, Go! The Numberland Rescue Team takes on a series of urgent missions for the Numberblobs.
Colour Group Concert. Pop star Lime is putting on a music show and invites groups of Colourblocks to perform onstage with her. But what do the members of the different groups have in common?
Movie Night. Love Monster leads his friends on an adventure through the Fluffytown Forest to make it in time for movie night, but he forgets to bring the movie.
Robert's Home Movies. During a rain shower, Justin and friends look back at their silliest moments.

items.t: Hey Duggee: Top of the Pups
items.sum: Building. Grab your hard hats and friends and join the building team!
Ball. Bing, Sula and Pando are kicking a ball around the garden. Sula does the best kick, but Bing kicks it the wrong way. As Bing kicks it back, he accidentally breaks Flop's window!
Fish. Dee encourages a friend to say 'fish', and we go on a whirlwind word adventure! We see lots of different fish - a flying fish, a goldfish and even some kissing fish!
Potion Commotion. Tralala and Batty's messy backyard potions turn out to be more magical than expected.
Mae, Bee and the Gnomad's Call. Da-Nono takes Mae to a Gnomad Moot to meet the other side of her family.
Body Song. Kiri sings a song about how wonderful it is to have your very own body.
More About Covering. Stop-motion preschool programme. The Twirlywoos watch a man as he covers his car in cleaning foam. Chickedy and Chick squirt foam everywhere.
Autumn. Educational series using Makaton sign language. Justin has lots of autumn fun with his friends, but Mr Tumble can't play football because leaves are blocking the goal.
Bottom Bump. Preschool series. The Teletubbies bottom-bounce on the Tubby Bouncy before wiggling their bottoms to a special bottom-bump song.
Mirror. Giovanna and Baby Bear invite babies and their grown-ups to explore mirrors through discovery, play, song and story. Babies and grown-ups at home can join in too!
Train Station. Elsee meets her new friend Amara at the train station and plays a game of I-spy.
Bloop Bloop. There is something fishy about the newest house guest, but Maddie and Triggs are determined to get to know the new arrival and figure out what makes him bloop.
Underwater Adventure. Is there an alien in the attic or is it just another fabulous transformation? A paper bowl becomes a sea turtle, boxes become boats and a bottle becomes a manta ray.
Go Bananas. Stop-frame animation featuring Raa Raa, who lives in the Jingly Jangly Jungle. Raa Raa and the others pick masses of lovely bananas for Ooo Ooo's banana party.
Chickenrat. It's bedtime, and Bingo can't remember where she left her beloved Floppy.
The Babysitting Badge. Duggee has a job to do outside the Clubhouse, but who will look after the Squirrels? King Tiger, of course, since he has his babysitting badge!

items.t: Chantelle and Rory's Teeny Tiny Creatures
items.sum: Woodpeckers. Rory and Sandy are in the woods to look for woodpeckers, whilst Chantelle meets a bird expert. Rory and Sandy try their hand at drumming just like a woodpecker.
Meet Ted's Family. Ted has big plans for his sister Sofia's birthday and organises a fun family tea party.
Flora the Fairy. The chefs are off to Granny Small's big birthday party, but Jen hasn't got a present.
Mission: Party Time. Disability dog Tinks is determined to help Charli feel confident enough to go to a party.
King Cobra and Sea Nettle Jellyfish. Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a king cobra and sea nettle jellyfish.
Lifeguard. Lifeguard Siobhan shows us how her rescue tube can help save someone who is struggling in the water.
Waffle's Club Camp Fun. It's After School Club Camp, but Waffle is far more interested in Mrs Hobbs's slippers.
A Noisy Neighbour. Oona tries to find a place for a noisy, little starling to sleep.
Cleo Nibbles. A soul singer is coming to perform in the garden, but no one knows what they look like.
Penguin Please. Declan causes a stir when he decides not to say 'please'.
The Together Team. Wilf wants to help the Piggies, but he can't stop falling asleep.
Fruit Salad. Children's animation. Welcome to the fabulous fruit factory, where Three's fruit-sorting machines aren't working. Find out how to split numbers into smaller numbers.
Zap. The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. Z likes a good snooze, filling the air with floaty zeds.
Hide-and-Seek. Ben meets his new friends at the park for a game of hide-and-seek. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble and Grandad get into a muddle.
Bunny Rabbits. Preschool series. Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po watch bunny rabbits. Bunny ears and tails appear on the Teletubbies, who do the bunny hop hop.
Blackbirds. Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers go on an eco quest to find out all about blackbirds.
Aeroplane and Trainers. Maddie finds out how pilots make aeroplanes take off and land, and she visits a factory where trainers are made.
Emergency Machines. Grace shows off three amazing machines, all made for emergencies.
Lantern Parade. Oliver and Felicity make lanterns with their faces on for the school's lantern parade.
Manatees. Animated deep sea adventures with Captain Barnacles and his explorers. Running out of air, Barnacles struggles to free his paw from the mouth of a giant clam.
The Tale of the Secret Treehouse. Animated series. Peter proves he has got what it takes to be part of the squirrel tribe when he competes for his own treetop hideout.
The Radio Badge. The Squirrels find some of Duggee's radio equipment and decide to start their own show.
Tall Tales. Brinicle gets a job as a news reporter but starts inventing stories to boost his ratings - until he realises his tall tales are misleading the other penguins.
How to Be a Supertato. In Tato Tower, Supertato shows the Grape Kids a film on how to be a Supertato like him.
Mission Playground. Weasy's toy car wrecks the Ducklings' playground, so they find an invention to stop him.
Rock-a-Bye Bo. Bo is tired and falls asleep in the middle of hunting for Fabio's lost inflatable fruit. It's up to Mojo to finish the job - without waking up poor, exhausted Bo!
Magic. Bluey teaches Bingo how to use magic so she can make Mum play with her.
